title: Redesign node fencing and graceful eviction for GPU fleet
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our current node lifecycle handling performs hard termination in a few code paths and relies on pod eviction fallthroughs. This has caused surprising tokenized request failures during autoscaler-driven scale-ins and complicated capacity planner reconciliation, producing sporadic 500s for short-lived workloads and long tail latency for chat workloads. Problem: - Orphaned allocations remain bound to drained nodes for up to 90s before reclaim, leading to capacity underutilization. - A hard fencing path (force-terminate containerized RTs) bypasses ordering (cache flush -> checkpoint -> eviction) and causes KV cache loss for active sessions. - The existing fencing/eviction logic is duplicated across lease-controller and binding controller causing inconsistent behavior and hard-to-follow race conditions. Goal: Redesign fencing + graceful eviction as a single well-tested module that: 1) Provides a soft-fence flow (mark node read-only, drain new requests, flush KV caches) then a timed hard-fence fallback; 2) Standardizes reclaim semantics so orphaned allocations are requeued for immediate placement; 3) Exposes observability metrics for every transition (fence_started, drain_completed, hard_fence_triggered, orphan_reclaimed) and integrates with capacity-planner snapshots; 4) Keeps fallback latency below 2x median pod termination time and eliminates request-level 500s from scale-in events.
acceptance_criteria: Soft-fence API deployed to canary cluster and used by autoscaler for 24h without production errors
Orphaned allocations reclaimed within 5s of drain completion in test workload (previously median 45s)
No request-level 500s attributable to node termination during controlled scale-ins in staging (0 occurrences across 10k requests)
New metrics emitted and surfaced in Console: node_fence_started, node_drain_completed, node_hard_fence, orphan_reclaims
Fallback hard-fence duration and retries documented and configurable via runtime-1.19 feature flag
implementation_steps: Audit current fencing/eviction code paths in lease-controller and gpu-fleet-controller and enumerate duplicated logic
Design soft-fence protocol: API, state transitions, TTLs, backoff rules, and KV cache flush hook with idempotency guarantees
Implement centralized node-fencer package in runtime repo with clear public interface and unit tests
Add requeue-on-orphan semantics to allocator: try-local-reassign -> immediate-requeue -> fallback routing
Integrate instrumentation (Prometheus counters + OpenTelemetry traces) and add Console dashboard panels
Create canary rollout plan and feature flag guarded deployment
Run controlled scale-in experiments on canary, then stage, then prod with load tests and chaos scenarios
Postmortem & doc updates: migration guide, operator runbook, and rollback steps
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Soft-fence introduces longer drain windows increasing short-term resource pressure. Mitigation: Add adaptive TTL based on current queue depth and run preflight load tests to tune defaults.

Risk: Requeue semantics may create request duplication for non-idempotent work. Mitigation: Require idempotency token at the API layer for reassignable allocations and add safeguards in allocator matching logic.

Risk: New code touches critical path for scale-in causing regressions. Mitigation: Feature-flag rollout, extensive unit/integration tests, and staged canary rollout with automatic rollback on SLO regression alerts.
notes_and_decisions: 2026-03-02: Decided to centralize fencing logic into a separate package rather than a controller mixin to reduce cross-controller coupling (decision by Aisha, Marcus, and Lina)
2026-03-05: Chose 5s reclaim target as initial SLO after benchmarking requeue latencies on t3/g5 clusters; will revisit after canary
2026-03-09: Opted to surface node_drain_completed via a dedicated trace span to make tail latency attribution easier in Console
qa_plan: Unit tests for node-fencer state machine covering all transitions and failure modes
Integration test: simulated scale-in in local k8s with 200 concurrent short-lived jobs verifying no 500s
E2E performance: run representative chat workload (median seq 512) across 3 scale-in patterns and measure request success and tail latency
Chaos test: random network partition between allocator and fencer to validate fallback hard-fence works as intended
rollout_plan: Week 1: Merge behind feature flag and deploy to dev clusters
Week 2: Canary on two runbooks (non-critical infra) for 72h, monitor fence/evict metrics
Week 3: Staging run for 48h with load test that mirrors customer traffic patterns
Week 4: Gradual prod rollout by region with automated SLO checks and ability to rollback traffic
Rollback: Toggle feature flag off and redeploy controllers; documented operator steps in runbook
